text:
simon: quick thread — sketching a per-tenant edge gateway to enforce data residency while allowing a controlled degraded-write mode during regional partitions. want quick feedback on tradeoffs and a tiny config sketch.

maria: curious — how's this different from the residency proxy we already have? :thinking:

simon: good q. differences: 1) edge gateway lives in the region and becomes the single local ingress for a tenant. 2) instead of blocking writes when the primary lease can't be reached, it can accept writes into a local encrypted escrow queue if the tenant opted in. 3) reconciliation is done with per-tenant monotonic sequence numbers + signed intents (not full db snapshots). goal is minimal cross-region IO for inference workloads.

nisha: split-brain avoidance? sounds risky to let multiple regions accept writes.

alex: plan = lease-first. normal case: tenant lease is held by region A -> gateway forwards. if lease unresponsive for Xs, region B's gateway MAY accept escrowed writes only if client flagged allow_degraded_writes=true and tenant residency policy permits. each escrowed write carries tenant-epoch and sequence id. on restore, we reconcile in order. last-writer-wins is NOT the default; we try deterministic merge for idempotent ops.

patrick: reconciliation detail: we should rely on per-tenant LSN + op-types that are idempotent. avoid large diffs by shipping only intents/ops. tombstones for deletes. avoid full table sync.

simon: config sketch (pseudo-YAML):
```
routing_policy:
  residency: required # required | preferred | none
  failover_behavior:
    allow_degraded_writes: false  # per-tenant default
    escrow_backend: regional-kv
    escrow_retention: 72h
    reconcile_strategy: monotonic-lsn
    max_escrow_size: 50MB
```

maria: testing plan? we need e2e sim of long partitions, model upgrades while partitions active, and KV reconciliation correctness. also latency targets for reads during degraded mode.

devops-bot: preview deployment for "edge-gateway/escrow" created — https://deploys.internal/edge-gateway/escrow-rc3 :rocket:

nisha: security questions — escrow data encryption + KMS usage? audit trail?

simon: escrow writes must be envelope-encrypted with tenant KMS keys (HSM-backed recommended). audit events (metadata only) are replicated to central audit pipeline; payload stays regional until reconciliation. ops must be able to prove signed intents.

alex: SLOs to propose: reads (local) <= 50ms P95, reads (remote fallback) <= 200ms P95; writes normally <= 100ms, degraded-write acceptance <= 150ms but flagged to client. reconciliation window SLA: eventual consistency within 24h for normal traffic, 72h max for heavy partitions.

patrick: SDK UX: require explicit flag e.g. `client.write({..., allow_degraded: true})` and expose response header `X-Redwood-Write-Mode: degraded|forwarded`. default should be to fail if residency requires strict writes.

maria: agree. also add server-side metric `escrow.ops` and `reconcile.conflicts` and a daily report for tenants that used degraded mode.

simon: one more operational note — during reconciliation run we should run a lightweight conflict detector first (per-tenant op counts, LSN gaps) and only escalate to human review if non-idempotent conflicts are detected. most inference workloads are append-ish so conflicts should be rare.

nisha: I'm concerned about legal/regulatory tenants. we need a policy that completely disables degraded writes for some tenants.

simon: yep — residency: required + allow_degraded_writes=false will cause write attempts to fail fast with 409 and client-facing error explaining region outage. SDK docs will show fallback patterns.

maria: sounds good. please capture this in an RFC with a dataflow diagram, reconciliation pseudocode, and test matrix. happy to co-author. :thumbsup:

simon: will draft RFC today and ping for reviewers. thanks all.
